name: Thought Record
lede: Catch the thought and look at it in daylight. One prompt at a time — skip anything that doesn't fit.
why: Writing a thought down separates having it from believing it. Noting where you were, what your body did, what you told yourself, and which pattern it fits turns a fog into something specific — and specific things can be worked with. Adapted in structure from standard CBT thought diaries; the prompts are our own and deliberately non-judgemental.

steps.prompt: Where were you, and what was happening?
steps.placeholder: e.g. Sunday night, alone, scrolling on my phone
examples: Sunday night, alone, scrolling on my phone
At work, just before a meeting
After a conversation that didn't go well

steps.prompt: How intense does it feel right now?

steps.help: Word for word if you can. Just catching it counts — you don't have to argue with it.
examples: Nothing I do makes a difference
It's going to go badly and it'll be my fault

steps.prompt: Does that thought fit any of these patterns?
steps.help: Naming the pattern is often where it loosens. Not a criticism — just useful information.
options: Catastrophising — jumping to the worst outcome
Mind reading — assuming I know what they think
All-or-nothing — total success or total failure
Should statements — I ought to be handling this
Emotional reasoning — it feels true, so it is
Filtering — only the bad part sticks

steps.prompt: Want to try one wider view?
options: What would I tell a friend?
Is this a fact, or a feeling?
What would I think about this in a week?

steps.prompt: A slightly wider way to hold it
steps.help: It doesn't have to be convincing. A crack of light is enough — tap an example if you're stuck.
examples: I'm comparing my worst day to other people's best
I don't have evidence for what they're thinking
This is a feeling, and feelings pass
One hard moment isn't the whole story
I'd be kinder about this if a friend told me

steps.prompt: And now — how intense does it feel?

nextSteps.label: Ground & Settle
nextSteps.because: Still running high. A short paced-breathing practice asks very little and often takes the edge off.

nextSteps.label: One Small Action
nextSteps.because: You've named it. One small action is a good way to not let it sit.
